SST voltage and power: The SSTs PCC voltages were maintained above 0.95 per unit as shown in Fig. 24(a). SST 2 reaches its max capacity during peak coincident charging while there is enough capacity remaining within other SSTs. Due to the active regulators and capacitors in the feeder, the SSTs MV terminal (PCC) voltages were within higher range and so the SSTs were not required to provide any significant reactive power support. There are only a few instances where the SSTs 1, 2 and 5 provided reactive power support. (a) (b) Figure 24. Fig. 25 (a) and (b) shows the MV and LV terminal voltages comparison for scenario with EV only and scenario with EV and SST. The black-dotted curve represents the regulated voltage at MV terminal with SST. Similarly, the SST also maintained the voltages at LV terminal at 1 per unit. These results show that SSTs help to improve and maintain the local voltages. (a) (b) Figure 25. They were designed to reduce the feeder peak hour demand by providing feeder peak hours energy consumption for the site. They are designed to support the site peak charging demand as well. PV generation is utilized to charge energy storage. The J1 feeder peak hours extend from 4 to 9 pm. Table 5 shows the capacity of PV and energy storage considered.
